acceptanceResults: The document maps entry points (CLI/MCP), observation/snapshot capture, Contract/policy/evidence validation, governance judgment, lifecycle transitions, command execution/scheduling, status/Outcome/human-decision projection, and persistence/recovery to their current authoritative source and owning file/function, with file:line citations.

The document cites concrete, line-referenced examples of duplicate fact reads across functions, functions that mix observation+decision+persistence, and any circular or one-directional dependency between lib.rs and governance_controls.rs/project_governance.rs.

The document names what is already well-separated and reusable as-is (e.g. RepositorySnapshot, RuntimeContext, the pure validators in governance_controls.rs, the capability-scoped file-I/O primitives) so later Work Items build on them instead of duplicating them.

For each of P1-B, P2-A, P2-B, P2-C, and P3, the document states the specific problem, the target responsibility boundary, the concrete compatibility risk, and how it would be verified -- without prescribing a full interface design.

The document states plainly where PhysicalSingleFlightCoordinator and the verification DAG/scheduler live relative to governance-decision code (crate-level separation already exists), as the factual basis for the P3 Work Item.
